implementation: Revalidate chosen target after submitting status and immediately before transport dispatch.
Reject old scene captures and expire accepted scene/object images through queueing and provider work using source and monotonic age.
Preserve pinned departure crops while comparing all-label rivals at capture and current verification time.
Reject newer target evidence and changed journal generations during final request/completion checks.
Keep missing, unobserved, ambiguous and matched outcomes distinct; retain readonly arrival verification.
Refuse conflicting current object views without falling through to older scene recall.
Expose failure_stage in status, snapshots, context and traces, plus per-case and aggregate fault reports.

first_full_suite.finding: One legacy approach test expected a queued verification task for an unavailable object verifier. Updated it to require immediate refusal with no task; terminal outcome remains unverified/unavailable.

limits: Synthetic RGB-D/unit fixtures and scripted providers do not measure real-model target or instance recognition accuracy.
Fault runs are sequential software contracts, not physical mission successes or concurrent stress coverage.
ROS attribution checks script resolution outcomes; they measure middleware status/snapshot delivery.
Any object-journal write during the final request check conservatively invalidates identity, even unrelated writes.
Default 5-second capture freshness can reject slow provider chains; held-out latency calibration remains open.
No paid provider, new Gazebo target-identity run, physical robot, installation matrix or endurance qualification performed.
